cards.title: Match creative-test volume to available budget
cards.claim: With a small daily budget, launching too many ads can leave new creatives without enough spend to produce a useful signal.
cards.action: Test a focused batch and give Facebook enough opportunity to distribute spend before judging the creatives.
applies_when: Creative testing has a relatively small daily budget.
New ads are receiving little or no spend.
do_not_use_when: There is sufficient budget to fund a larger test while still giving each ad meaningful delivery.
unknowns: No minimum spend per ad or required test duration is specified.
evidence_quotes: "You have to match your creative testing volume to your budget."
"So, if you're spending 30, 50, $100 a day, you can't feed an unlimited number of ads enough spend to actually learn anything."
"I'd rather test a focused batch and give Facebook enough opportunity to distribute spend and give me some kind of signal."

cards.title: Compare creative variants with equal visibility
cards.claim: An ad driving the most sales is not necessarily the best creative if it was the only ad that received spend.
cards.action: Test alternative ads in an apples-to-apples environment, allow equal visibility, then use the data to identify why one performed better.
applies_when: Comparing creative concepts such as UGC versus carousel.
Platform delivery is concentrating spend on one ad.
do_not_use_when: The variants differ across multiple uncontrolled variables and cannot be compared apples-to-apples.
unknowns: The passage does not specify the campaign setup or method used to ensure equal visibility.
evidence_quotes: "I don't really crown something a winner just because it drives the most of your sales."
"it's the only thing that got spend. So, of course it's driving sales."
"make sure you test them in an apples-to-apples environment like this creative test and allow them to get equal visibility and then look at the data to identify why something was better."
"Don't just let one ad get the spend and assume that this is your winner."

cards.title: Assess creative across the customer journey, not CTR alone
cards.claim: A visually engaging creative can earn high CTR without leading to buying behavior when it does not communicate the product or value; a lower-CTR ad that shows the routine, before-and-after, application, and product may produce more buying behavior in this example.
cards.action: Review attention, clicks to site, and post-click behavior alongside CPA and return on ad spend when determining why a creative won or lost.
applies_when: A creative has strong engagement or CTR but weak buying behavior.
Comparing ads that differ in how clearly they communicate product value.
do_not_use_when: Only CTR or sales volume is available and delivery was not comparable between ads.
unknowns: The reported 10.9% and 6.3 figures are not fully labeled in the passage.
The example's final return outcome is not yet established because the test is still running.
evidence_quotes: "We have a 10.9%. This is actually like a very high CTR for e-commerce, but it almost doesn't matter because look at the supporting metrics here. It led to very little buying behavior"
"this video actually showed the routine. It showed the before and after. It showed how to apply the product. It showed what you're actually buying."
"Please don't look to just CPA. There's a lot more to the story than just return on ad spend and CPA."
"Then we ask, did they click to the site?"
